served;\n    }, TaskCreationOptions.LongRunning);\n\n    internal static void RoundTrip(string endpoint, int length, uint seed, Framing framing = Framing.HalfClose)\n    {\n        using var client = IpcTransports.Connect(endpoint);\n        var sent = Payload(length, seed);\n        var writer = Task.Factory.StartNew(() =>\n        {\n            var output = client.Clone();\n            if (framing == Framing.LengthPrefix)\n            {\n                output.Write(BitConverter.GetBytes((long)sent.Length));\n            }\n            output.Write(sent);\n            output.Flush();\n            if (framing == Framing.HalfClose)\n            {\n                output.CloseWrite();\n            }\n        }, TaskCreationOptions.LongRunning);\n        byte[] echoed;\n        if (framing == Framing.HalfClose)\n        {\n            using var buffer = new MemoryStream();\n            client.CopyTo(buffer);\n            echoed = buffer.ToArray();\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            echoed = new byte[length];\n            client.ReadExactly(echoed);\n        }\n        writer.GetAwaiter().GetResult();\n        Assert.Equal(sent.Length, echoed.Length);\n        Assert.True(sent.AsSpan().SequenceEqual(echoed), $\"{endpoint}: echoed bytes differ\");\n        client.Shutdown();\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>Two consecutive and two concurrent connections echo their It also reads `.lenv` and `.env` first, as the Rust one does.\n- **Embedded store.** It writes the same files on disk as Rust (the `doublets` unit store, the names sidecar, the transitions and version-control logs), so either implementation opens the other's stores. The embedded API includes:\n  - `NamedTypesDecorator.open` and `QueryProcessor`;\n  - the decorators for transactions with crash recovery, version control, persistent transformations (triggers) and permissions, plus triplets over doublets;\n  - the advisory `<db>.lock` lock, taken with `flock` or `LockFileEx` through `node:ffi`/`bun:ffi`, or `Deno.FsFile.lock`, so a JavaScript process and a Rust process exclude each other.\n- **File-backed `DoubletsStorage`.** `DoubletsStorage.open` / `openShared` / `openExclusive` port the Rust `DoubletsStorage<usize, FileMappedUnitStore<usize>>` over a JavaScript port of the `doublets` unit store (`unit-store*.js`, `u64` and `u32` addresses). The links are changed in place and written through on every operation, so the file is byte for byte the one Rust writes. `TransactionsDecorator` writes through it directly, as `rust/examples/embedded_store.rs` does. `examples/embedded-store/embedded-store.mjs` produces the same `db.links` as the Rust example on Node.js, Bun and Deno. A `u64` address above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` fails with `AddressOverflowError` instead of being rounded.\n- **Serving.** It has the protocol server (`--serve`), the relay (`--forward`) and the client (`--connect`), over TCP and every IPC kind the runtimes support, and the GraphQL endpoint for Deep (`--serve ADDR --graphql`).\n- **Parity.** Every `javascript` cell in `parity/features.json` is now `implemented` and points at js/server's sources and tests. JavaScript is the third suite that must load all 41 golden fixtures.\n\n`js-server.yml` runs behind the JavaScript stage:\n- the unit tests with 100 % line, branch and function coverage on Node.js, then on Bun and Deno;\n- the unit tests on Linux, macOS and Windows with Node.js 20, 22 and 26;\n- the embedded store example on Node.js, Bun and Deno, whose `db.links` files must be identical;\n- the golden unit-store files (`test/fixtures/unit-store-*.links`, written by the Rust `unit_store_trace` driver) and a differential unit-store test that replays random operations through the Rust driver and the JavaScript store and compares every byte;\n- the differential tests, which run each invocation through the Rust `clink` and through `bin/clink.js` and compare stdout, stderr, the exit status and every file written;\n- the client's conformance scenarios against this package's `clink --serve` (`CLINK_JS`);\n- the npm release.\n\nDebug switches: `clink --trace`, `CLINK_IPC_TRACE=1`, `CLINK_DIFFERENTIAL_DEBUG=1`.\n\n**Human action for the first npm release:** add this repository and `js-server.yml` as a trusted publisher of `@link-foundation/link-cli-server` on npmjs.com. Resending the end then failed with \"the peer hung up\", which crashed the C# test host. All three now treat that failure as the peer hanging up, which ends the stream normally. C# passed in CI after the fix.\n\n2. **Deno failure in the JavaScript store.** A flush tells other processes the file changed by setting its modification time to now. JavaScript's clock only has millisecond resolution, so a flush in the same millisecond as the previous change looked like no change. Deno also stores about half of all times one millisecond early. The flush now always sets a time in a later millisecond than the current one, and requests the middle of that millisecond so Deno keeps it. Before the fix the Deno tests failed in CI and in 1 of 6 local runs; afterwards they passed 20 of 20 locally and in CI. The probe I used to confirm Deno's behaviour is saved in `experiments/issue-111/futimes-millisecond-truncation.mjs`.\n\nBoth bugs are recorded in the case study, the Rust and C# release notes, and the PR description.\n\nThe first npm release of `@link-foundation/link-cli-server` needs one manual step: add this repository and `js-server.yml` as a trusted publisher on npmjs.com, or publish the first version by hand. Until then the npm release job fails with a message saying exactly that."

C# passed in CI after the fix.\n\n2. **Deno failure in the JavaScript store.** A flush tells other processes the file changed by setting its modification time to now. JavaScript's clock only has millisecond resolution, so a flush in the same millisecond as the previous change looked like no change. Deno also stores about half of all times one millisecond early. The flush now always sets a time in a later millisecond than the current one, and requests the middle of that millisecond so Deno keeps it. Before the fix the Deno tests failed in CI and in 1 of 6 local runs; afterwards they passed 20 of 20 locally and in CI. The probe I used to confirm Deno's behaviour is saved in `experiments/issue-111/futimes-millisecond-truncation.mjs`.\n\nBoth bugs are recorded in the case study, the Rust and C# release notes, and the PR description.\n\nThe first npm release of `@link-foundation/link-cli-server` needs one manual step: add this repository and `js-server.yml` as a trusted publisher on npmjs.com, or publish the first version by hand. Problem\n\nlink-cli has three implementations (C# in `csharp/`, Rust in `rust/`, and a JavaScript/WASM web workbench in `js/`) and one workflow per stack. The workflows do not wait for each other, nothing in CI checks that the C# and Rust implementations stay at parity, `main` has no protection, and the open pull requests are stale or red. This is the audit of link-cli against the standard in link-assistant/router#759 (requirements 3, 4, 6 and 8), the shared pipeline templates and `hive-mind/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`. Only missing or broken practices are listed.\n\n## Findings\n\n1. **Rust and C# CI/CD are not gated on JavaScript.** `.github/workflows/rust.yml`, `csharp.yml` and `wasm.yml` each trigger on their own `push`/`pull_request` and none has `workflow_run` or a cross-workflow `needs:`. The JavaScript unit tests (`npm run test:js`) run only in `wasm.yml` (line 81), which itself builds the Rust WASM crate. A Rust or C# change starts the full Rust matrix and the C# matrix in parallel with the JavaScript checks. Evidence from the run list: for the Dependabot branch `dependabot/nuget/...` on 2026-10-09 `C# CI/CD Pipeline`, `Dependencies`, `Docs` and `Security` all started at the same second (03:49:35Z).\n2. **No parity gate between the implementations.** There is no parity manifest and no checker. The only parity artefacts are one Rust test file (`rust/tests/query_processor_csharp_parity_tests.rs`) and prose in `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`. Nothing fails CI when a feature changes in C# but not in Rust (or the reverse). The `js/` package is a React/WASM workbench over the Rust crate, and no document states which features it covers. Path filters make this worse: `rust.yml` runs only for `rust/**` and `csharp.yml` only for C# paths, so a one-sided change never triggers the other stack's checks.\n3. **`main` is not protected.** `gh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/branches/main/protection` returns 404 \"Branch not protected\", and `gh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/rulesets` returns an empty list. No required checks, so a red PR can be merged and the three stages are not enforced.\n4. **Eight stale pull requests from 2025 are still open.** #36, #37, #38, #39, #40, #41 (all 2025-09-10), #49 (2025-09-10) and #57 (2025-09-15). They are about 13 months old, none has a CI check result, and each duplicates an open issue (#30-#35, #18, #56, #59, #60). There is no stale policy or workflow that closes or flags them.\n5. **The only active PR and the default branch are red.** PR #109 (Dependabot, NuGet group, opened 2026-10-09) fails `C# CI/CD Pipeline`: `LinoProtocolCodecTests.ReferencesAreQuotedOnlyWhenNeeded` and `TextMessagesAreDotStuffed` fail on Windows and in \"Simulate Fresh Merge\", which reports a semantic merge conflict. The `Dependencies` workflow also failed on `main` on 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-09 (daily scheduled runs) and nobody has acted on it.\n6. **Files and workflows from the shared templates are missing.** Compared with `rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` and `js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`, link-cli has none of: `.github/workflows/workflows.yml` (actionlint with shellcheck), `.github/zizmor.yml` (workflow security lint), `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md`. That new commit carries no checks, so any rule that requires checks rejects it:\n\n- Classic protection with required checks exempts only administrators, and `GITHUB_TOKEN` is not one.\n- Making GitHub Actions a ruleset bypass actor is what the hive-mind CI/CD guide suggests. GitHub refuses it for this repository with HTTP 422 \"Actor GitHub Actions integration must be part of the ruleset source or owner organization\" ([evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/case-studies/issue-111/data/actions-bypass-422.json); `experiments/issue-111/probe-actions-bypass.sh` reproduces it).\n\nSo the ruleset's only bypass actor is deploy keys. A write deploy key was added, and its private key is the `RELEASE_DEPLOY_KEY` secret of a new `release` environment that only `main` can deploy to. The four release jobs run in that environment and check out with `ssh-key`. Their trusted publishing is unaffected: crates.io and NuGet check the OIDC environment claim only when a policy names an environment. `ci-governance.test.mjs` checks the four jobs. If the key is ever missing, both release scripts stop before tagging with a message that says how to restore it, and [troubleshooting](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md#a-release-push-was-declined) has the commands.\n\nUntil this PR merges, `main` still runs the old release jobs, which push with `GITHUB_TOKEN`. A release triggered by another merge before then is declined by the ruleset and fails with that explicit message. The release after this PR merges uses the deploy key.\n\n### How to verify\n\n```sh\ngh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/branches/main/protection -i | head -1    # HTTP/2.0 200 OK\ngh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/rules/branches/main --jq '.[].parameters.required_status_checks[]?.context'\nnpm --prefix js ci && npm --prefix js run lint && npm --prefix js run test:js\nnode parity/check-parity.mjs --base origin/main --verbose\n```\n\n### Debugging aids\n\n`PARITY_DEBUG` / `--verbose`, `STACK_PATHS_DEBUG`, `TRACKING_ISSUE_DEBUG`, and `TRACKING_ISSUE_DRY_RUN`. CI turns each one on when a job is re-run with debug logging. They are listed in [docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md#debug-switches).\n\n### JavaScript server and embedded implementation\n\nThe owner's review asks for a full JavaScript server/embedded implementation next to the client. `js/server` is `@link-foundation/link-cli-server`: the Rust `clink` in plain JavaScript, with no WebAssembly or native code, for Node.js 20+, Bun and Deno on Linux, macOS and Windows ([README](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/js/server/README.md)).\n\n- **Command line.** `bin/clink.js` takes every option of the Rust `clink` and prints the same output, errors and exit codes. It also reads `.lenv` and `.env` first, as the Rust one does.\n- **Embedded store.** It writes the same files on disk as Rust (the `doublets` unit store, the names sidecar, the transitions and version-control logs), so either implementation opens the other's stores. The embedded API includes:\n  - `NamedTypesDecorator.open` and `QueryProcessor`;\n  - the decorators for transactions with crash recovery, version control, persistent transformations (triggers) and permissions, plus triplets over doublets;\n  - the advisory `<db>.lock` lock, taken with `flock` or `LockFileEx` through `node:ffi`/`bun:ffi`, or `Deno.FsFile.lock`, so a JavaScript process and a Rust process exclude each other.\n- **File-backed `DoubletsStorage`.** `DoubletsStorage.open` / `openShared` / `openExclusive` port the Rust `DoubletsStorage<usize, FileMappedUnitStore<usize>>` over a JavaScript port of the `doublets` unit store (`unit-store*.js`, `u64` and `u32` addresses). The links are changed in place and written through on every operation, so the file is byte for byte the one Rust writes. `TransactionsDecorator` writes through it directly, as `rust/examples/embedded_store.rs` does. `examples/embedded-store/embedded-store.mjs` produces the same `db.links` as the Rust example on Node.js, Bun and Deno. A `u64` address above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` fails with `AddressOverflowError` instead of being rounded.\n- **Serving.** It has the protocol server (`--serve`), the relay (`--forward`) and the client (`--connect`), over TCP and every IPC kind the runtimes support, and the GraphQL endpoint for Deep (`--serve ADDR --graphql`).\n- **Parity.** Every `javascript` cell in `parity/features.json` is now `implemented` and points at js/server's sources and tests. JavaScript is the third suite that must load all 41 golden fixtures.\n\n`js-server.yml` runs behind the JavaScript stage:\n- the unit tests with 100 % line, branch and function coverage on Node.js, then on Bun and Deno;\n- the unit tests on Linux, macOS and Windows with Node.js 20, 22 and 26;\n- the embedded store example on Node.js, Bun and Deno, whose `db.links` files must be identical;\n- the golden unit-store files (`test/fixtures/unit-store-*.links`, written by the Rust `unit_store_trace` driver) and a differential unit-store test that replays random operations through the Rust driver and the JavaScript store and compares every byte;\n- the differential tests, which run each invocation through the Rust `clink` and through `bin/clink.js` and compare stdout, stderr, the exit status and every file written;\n- the client's conformance scenarios against this package's `clink --serve` (`CLINK_JS`);\n- the npm release.\n\nDebug switches: `clink --trace`, `CLINK_IPC_TRACE=1`, `CLINK_DIFFERENTIAL_DEBUG=1`.\n\n**Human action for the first npm release:** add this repository and `js-server.yml` as a trusted publisher of `@link-foundation/link-cli-server` on npmjs.com. If the package does not exist yet, a maintainer publishes the first version by hand. Until then the release job fails with a message that says exactly this.\n\n### Fixes found by CI\n\nC# run [43635026592](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/43635026592) crashed its test host with `IpcException: the peer hung up`, thrown from `CloseWrite` on a System V queue. A peer that reads EOF and hangs up removes both queues, its ACK and ABORT included. A retransmitted EOF then fails with `EIDRM` (`ConnectionReset`) instead of reading the ABORT. Rust (`datagram.rs`), C# (`DatagramSession.cs`) and the JS server (`ipc-datagram.js`) now treat that failure while sending the end as a hang-up, as they already did for an ABORT. Regression tests use a link that vanishes on EOF: `a_peer_removing_the_link_before_the_end_is_acknowledged_still_ends_the_stream`, `APeerRemovingTheLinkBeforeTheEndIsAcknowledgedStillEndsTheStream`, and the matching `ipc-datagram.test.mjs` case. Each failed before the fix and passes with it. The JS client already traces and ignores send failures.\n\nThe Deno unit tests of `js-server.yml` for 5a7064a5 found that `DoubletsStorage.flush` could keep the old revision. It set the modification time to `new Date()`, which has only milliseconds. Deno 2.9 also truncates the time it is given to whole milliseconds and stores about half of all Dates one millisecond early ([`futimes-millisecond-truncation.mjs`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/experiments/issue-111/futimes-millisecond-truncation.mjs)). The flush now asks for the middle of a millisecond later than the current modification time. The regression test 'publishes a later revision even within the millisecond of the last one' fails before the change. Both findings are root causes 15 and 16 in the [case
